title: Lemon herb chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Line two large baking trays; six portions need room to roast rather than steam.
Mix lemon juice, oil, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Pat chicken dry and coat it with half the mixture; do not wash raw chicken.
Toss potatoes and broccoli with the remaining mixture. Roast potatoes for 10 minutes first, then add chicken and broccoli in a single layer on the trays.
Roast another 20–30 minutes, turning vegetables halfway. Check the thickest chicken pieces with a thermometer: they must reach 165°F / 74°C.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes. Divide chicken and vegetables among six plates and spoon over the cooked pan juices.
note: Use separate utensils for raw chicken and ready-to-eat food. Timing depends on the thickness of the chicken.

photo.author: Rajeeb Dutta
photo.alt: Roasted chicken leg piece-MB20 (illustrative photo)

title: Peanut butter apple bites
steps: Wash apples, remove cores and slice each into eight wedges, making 24 pieces.
Mix lemon juice and water in a bowl. Dip apple wedges briefly, then drain and pat dry to slow browning.
Stir peanut butter to loosen it. Spread about 5 g on each wedge; avoid thick spoonfuls for young children.
Sprinkle evenly with oats and cinnamon. Put four wedges on each of six plates.
Serve promptly for the best texture, or cover and refrigerate until serving.
note: For small children, use thin apple slices or softened apple and an age-appropriate thin spread.

photo.author: State Government Photographer
photo.alt: Sliced apples(GN01158) (illustrative photo)

title: Tomato basil pasta

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.amount: 1 tsp, plus pasta water as needed

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Prepare the garlic and tear the basil; reserve a few leaves for serving.
Heat oil in a wide pan over medium-low heat. Cook garlic for 1–2 minutes until fragrant, without browning.
Add tomatoes, salt and pepper. Simmer gently, uncovered, for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally until slightly thickened.
Cook pasta according to the package until al dente. Reserve 250 mL cooking water before draining.
Toss pasta with sauce over low heat for 1–2 minutes. Add reserved water a little at a time until the sauce coats the pasta.
Fold in basil off the heat. Divide into six bowls; add Parmesan if desired.
note: Use gluten-free pasta if needed. The pasta-water quantity is a reserve, not an amount you must add.

photo.author: Missvain
photo.alt: Bottega Louie - February 2024 - Sarah Stierch 03 (illustrative photo)

title: Berry yogurt parfait
steps: Rinse berries, drain well and cut large strawberries into bite-size pieces.
Stir yogurt with lemon zest. Add honey only if needed; omit honey for children under one year.
Set out six glasses or small bowls. Add 75 g yogurt, 50 g berries and 15 g granola to each.
Repeat those layers once, using all the ingredients evenly.
Serve immediately to keep granola crisp, or refrigerate the yogurt and fruit layers and add granola just before serving.
allergens: Milk; granola may contain wheat, nuts or sesame
note: Each serving has 150 g yogurt, 100 g fruit and 30 g granola.

photo.author: User:Mattes
photo.alt: Parfait desert (illustrative photo)

title: Ginger salmon rice bowl
steps: Rinse rice and cook with the package-specified water in a rice cooker or covered pot.
Heat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Mix soy sauce, ginger, vinegar and oil; brush onto salmon in a lined baking dish.
Bake salmon for about 12–18 minutes, depending on thickness, until the center reaches 145°F / 63°C.
Meanwhile, steam broccoli and carrots for 5–8 minutes until tender but still colorful.
Fluff rice and divide it among six bowls. Add vegetables and one salmon portion per bowl.
Serve immediately. Any marinade that touched raw fish must be discarded or brought to a full boil before use.
allergens: Fish; soy; wheat in some soy sauces
note: Use tamari certified gluten-free if needed. Do not use raw-fish marinade as a cold dressing.

photo.author: BlessNathan
photo.alt: Rice, beans and Salmon Fish (illustrative photo)

title: Sesame edamame
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add frozen edamame and cook for the time specified on its package, typically 4–6 minutes.
Check that beans are hot and tender; drain thoroughly.
Toss warm pods with sesame oil and salt in a large bowl.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and divide into six small bowls.
Squeeze beans out of the pods to eat. Discard pods; they are not edible.
note: The 900 g quantity includes pods; the edible bean weight is lower.

photo.author: yomi955
photo.alt: Edamame on a bamboo bowl by yomi955 (illustrative photo)

title: Chickpea vegetable bowl
steps: Drain and rinse chickpeas. Measure the drained weight, rather than the weight printed for a full can including liquid.
Wash cucumber and tomatoes; cut into 1 cm pieces. Finely chop parsley.
Whisk oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a large serving bowl.
Add chickpeas, vegetables and parsley. Toss gently until coated and let stand for 10 minutes.
Divide the salad among six bowls. Serve each with one pita, warmed if desired.
note: For a gluten-free meal, replace pita with cooked rice or certified gluten-free bread.

photo.author: Geoff Peters from Vancouver, BC, Canada
photo.alt: Chick pea salad (5045986717) (illustrative photo)

title: Lemony hummus
steps: Drain and rinse chickpeas. Wash vegetables and cut into sticks for dipping.
Blend tahini and lemon juice for 30 seconds. Add garlic, chickpeas and salt; blend until mostly smooth.
With the machine running, add 90 mL cold water gradually. Scrape down the sides, then add more water only as needed for a soft dip.
Blend in 15 mL oil. Taste and adjust lemon or salt if desired.
Divide hummus among six dishes, drizzle with the remaining oil and serve with vegetable sticks.
note: Makes roughly 1 kg hummus: a generous shared snack for six, with possible leftovers.

photo.author: Satdeep Gill
photo.alt: Homemade hummus and pita 03 (illustrative photo)

title: Tofu and vegetable stir-fry
steps: Drain tofu, pat dry and cut into 2 cm cubes. Slice vegetables into similar-size pieces.
Mix soy sauce, cornstarch and water until no lumps remain.
Heat half the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown tofu in two batches, about 3–4 minutes per side; remove to a plate.
Add remaining oil, ginger and garlic. Stir for 30 seconds, then add carrots and broccoli; stir-fry for 4 minutes. Add peppers and cook another 2–3 minutes.
Return tofu to the pan. Stir the sauce again, pour it in and simmer for 1–2 minutes until it thickens and coats everything.
Divide cooked rice among six bowls and top with the stir-fry. Cook in batches if the pan is crowded.
allergens: Soy; wheat in some soy sauces
note: Cook rice fresh or reheat previously chilled rice thoroughly; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.

photo.author: Archon6812
photo.alt: Billyfoodmabodofu3 (illustrative photo)

title: Steamed sweet potato
steps: Scrub sweet potatoes under running water. Trim ends and cut into uniform 3 cm rounds.
Fill the steamer base with water below the basket and bring it to a boil.
Arrange pieces in the basket with small gaps; use two tiers if needed. Cover tightly.
Steam for 20–25 minutes. A knife should slide through the thickest piece easily; add more time for larger pieces.
Remove carefully, let cool for 3–5 minutes and divide into six portions of about 200 g raw-weight equivalent.
allergens: No major allergens in listed ingredients
note: Check the water level during cooking; add hot water if needed without letting the pot boil dry.

photo.author: Shark2025
photo.alt: Cooked sweet potatoes (illustrative photo)

title: Three-cup mushroom chicken
steps: Cut chicken into 3 cm pieces; halve mushrooms. Prepare ginger, garlic and basil before heating the pan.
Heat sesame oil over medium heat. Add ginger and garlic and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant, avoiding scorching.
Add chicken in batches and brown for 3–4 minutes per batch. Return all chicken to the pan and add mushrooms.
Pour in soy sauce, rice wine and water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Check that chicken reaches 165°F / 74°C. Uncover and simmer another 3–5 minutes to reduce the sauce.
Turn off heat and fold in basil until wilted. Serve with rice in six portions.
allergens: Soy; sesame; wheat in some soy sauces
note: This home version uses less oil than traditional versions. For an alcohol-free version, replace wine with water; simmering does not guarantee all alcohol is removed.

photo.author: Ceeseven
photo.alt: Three Cup Chicken in Clay Pot (illustrative photo)

title: Scallion egg pancake
steps: Check the pancake package for its cooking time and any thawing instructions.
Beat eggs with scallions. Divide the mixture mentally into six equal portions.
Heat 5 mL oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat. Cook one pancake according to its package until golden on both sides.
Lift the pancake out. Pour in one-sixth of the egg mixture, then place the pancake over the wet egg.
Cook until the egg is fully set. Flip briefly if needed, then roll or cut into wedges.
Repeat for the remaining five pancakes. Serve one per person, with optional soy sauce.
allergens: Wheat; egg; soy if using sauce
note: Use two pans to shorten cooking time. Keep finished pancakes warm rather than letting raw egg sit out.

photo.author: Infrogmation of New Orleans
photo.alt: Plate of scallion pancakes (illustrative photo)

title: Tomato egg rice
steps: Wash tomatoes and cut into wedges. Slice scallions and beat eggs with half the salt.
Heat half the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add eggs, gently fold into soft curds and cook until set; transfer to a plate.
Add remaining oil and tomatoes. Cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until they release juice.
Add water, remaining salt and optional sugar. Cover and simmer 5–7 minutes until tomatoes soften.
Return eggs to the pan, fold gently and heat through for 1–2 minutes. Scatter over scallions.
Serve in six bowls over hot cooked rice.
note: Avoid high heat after adding eggs back; it can make the curds rubbery.

photo.author: NNU-10-24100123
photo.alt: Stir Fried Tomatoes with Scrambled Eggs (illustrative photo)

title: Mango coconut cups
steps: Peel mangoes, cut away the stones and weigh 900 g edible flesh. Dice most of it; mash 150 g with lime juice.
Stir the mashed mango into coconut yogurt until evenly combined.
Place 75 g diced mango into each of six glasses. Add 125 g mango yogurt to each.
Top with the remaining diced mango, divided equally, and 5 g shredded coconut per cup.
Cover and refrigerate for 20 minutes if you prefer a chilled dessert; serve within the product storage guidance.
allergens: Coconut; check yogurt for milk, soy or other allergens
note: No gelatin is used; this is a layered fruit dessert rather than a set pudding. Chilling time is optional and additional.

photo.author: Ceeseven
photo.alt: Mango Pudding with Strawberry Sauce (illustrative photo)

title: Vegetable bibimbap
steps: Cook rice according to its package. Prepare each vegetable separately so their colors and textures remain distinct.
Heat a little neutral oil over medium heat. Sauté carrots and zucchini separately for 3–4 minutes each until tender; set aside.
Sauté mushrooms for 5–6 minutes until softened. Wilt spinach for 1–2 minutes and squeeze out excess liquid when cool enough to handle.
Mix gochujang, water and sesame oil into a spoonable sauce.
Cook six eggs in the remaining oil until whites and yolks are firm.
Divide rice among six bowls. Arrange vegetables and an egg on each, add sauce to taste and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Mix everything together at the table before eating.
allergens: Egg; sesame; soy and wheat may be in gochujang
note: For a milder bowl, serve gochujang on the side. Package sauces vary in salt and heat.

photo.author: Andy Li
photo.alt: Vegan hot stone pot bibimbap (Dolsot-bibimbap) - Kogi 2023-10-16 (illustrative photo)

title: Mini vegetable pancakes
steps: Wash and shred vegetables finely. Gently squeeze zucchini to remove excess water.
Whisk flour, water and salt into a smooth batter; fold in carrots, zucchini and scallions.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Spoon in small portions and flatten to about 8 cm wide.
Cook 3–4 minutes per side until golden and the center is set, without wet flour. Work in batches and replenish oil as needed.
Drain briefly on a rack. Mix soy sauce and vinegar for dipping.
Make about 18 small pancakes and serve three per person with sauce on the side.
note: Small, thin pancakes cook more evenly than thick ones. Keep batter stirred between batches.

photo.author: Infrogmation of New Orleans
photo.alt: Plate of scallion pancakes (illustrative photo)

title: Red lentil dal
steps: Rinse lentils until the water runs mostly clear. Put them in a large saucepan with water and turmeric.
Bring to a boil, skim foam if needed, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook partly covered for 20–25 minutes, stirring so the bottom does not stick.
In another pan, heat oil over medium heat. Add cumin seeds for 30 seconds, then onion and cook for 5–7 minutes.
Add ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then tomatoes. Cook for 6–8 minutes until softened.
Stir the tomato mixture and salt into the lentils. Simmer 5 minutes, adding hot water if too thick.
The finished dal should be soft and spoonable. Divide among six bowls and serve with rice.
allergens: No major allergens in listed ingredients
note: Lentils absorb different amounts of water; adjust gradually. This is a mild family version.

photo.author: Pelican
photo.alt: Dal soup (Indian lentil dish) (illustrative photo)

title: Cucumber raita
steps: Wash cucumber, halve lengthwise and remove watery seeds if large. Coarsely grate the flesh.
Squeeze the grated cucumber gently in a clean towel so the dip does not become watery.
Whisk yogurt until smooth, then stir in cucumber, cumin, mint, salt and pepper.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Cover and chill for at least 15 minutes if time allows.
Divide among six bowls, about 200 g each, and serve as a cooling snack or side.
note: Keep refrigerated. Chilling time is additional; use unsweetened plant yogurt if avoiding dairy.

photo.author: Miansari66
photo.alt: Kafta Raita (illustrative photo)

title: Autumn squash tray bake

ingredients.name: Butternut squash, peeled and seeded weight

steps: Heat oven to 425°F / 220°C. Line two large trays so vegetables can spread out.
Peel and seed squash carefully, then cut into 2 cm cubes. Cut onions into wedges; drain and rinse chickpeas.
Toss squash and onion with oil, rosemary, salt and pepper. Spread evenly across the trays.
Roast for 20 minutes, then stir and add chickpeas. Roast another 15–20 minutes until squash is fork-tender and browned at the edges.
Switch tray positions halfway through if one browns faster. Divide among six plates.
Serve each portion with a slice of whole-grain bread.
note: Weigh squash after peeling and seeding. A crowded tray gives softer, less browned vegetables.

photo.author: Valereee
photo.alt: Roasted honeynut squash (illustrative photo)

title: Warm cinnamon pears
steps: Wash pears, halve and remove cores. Slice each half into three thick wedges.
Put water, cinnamon and lemon juice in a wide pan. Add pears in a single layer where possible.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Cover and cook 8–12 minutes until a knife enters easily; firmer pears may need longer.
Uncover and simmer 2–3 minutes to reduce the liquid slightly. Stir gently to avoid breaking the wedges.
Divide pears among six bowls with a little warm cooking liquid. Add 75 g yogurt per portion.
Drizzle with optional honey only for diners older than one year and serve warm.
note: This gently poached version keeps the fruit soft; it is not a caramelized or baked pear recipe.

photo.author: Infrogmation of New Orleans
photo.alt: Poached Pears in bowl (illustrative photo)

title: Autumn Harvest Turkey Meatballs
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper. Toss potatoes with 20 mL oil and 2 g salt on a separate rimmed tray; roast for 10 minutes before adding the meatballs.
In a large bowl, gently combine turkey, cranberries, breadcrumbs, egg, sage, salt, and pepper until just mixed; do not overwork.
Shape the mixture into 18 equal meatballs, approximately 60g each.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the meatballs in batches for 5 minutes, turning carefully.
Transfer browned meatballs to the prepared baking sheet. Pour chicken broth into the pan to deglaze, then pour over the meatballs.

Bake for 15-20 minutes until the center of the meatballs reaches 165°F / 74°C. Continue roasting potatoes until tender, about 30-40 minutes total. Toss green beans with the remaining vegetable oil and salt and add to the potato tray for its final 15 minutes.
Remove from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes. Serve three meatballs per person with pan juices. Divide the roasted potatoes and green beans among the six plates.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; consume within 3-4 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C.
note: The cranberries add a subtle sweetness perfect for the October season. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4 days. Not recommended for freezing due to texture changes.

photo.author: روتانا
photo.alt: Autumn Harvest Turkey Meatballs — illustrative photo

title: Maple Glazed Roasted Pumpkin Seeds
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F / 175°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Rinse seeds thoroughly and pat completely dry with a clean kitchen towel to ensure crunchiness.
In a medium bowl, toss the dry seeds with melted butter, maple syrup, nutmeg, and salt until evenly coated.
Spread the seeds in a single layer on the baking sheet, ensuring they do not overlap.
Roast for 20-25 minutes, stirring every 8 minutes to prevent burning and ensure even caramelization.
Remove when seeds are deep golden brown. They will continue to crisp up as they cool.
Divide into six small bowls, approximately 50g each.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days; if they lose crispness, re-toast in the oven for 3 minutes.
note: Best enjoyed as a crunchy seasonal snack. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Cool completely, then keep in an airtight jar at room temperature for up to 5 days.

photo.author: Daniel Schwen
photo.alt: Maple Glazed Roasted Pumpkin Seeds — illustrative photo

title: Rustic Root Vegetable Cottage Pie
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Boil potatoes in water with half the measured salt until tender, then mash with butter and milk.
In a large skillet, brown the beef with onions and carrots over medium-high heat until the meat reaches 160°F / 71°C.
Stir in tomato paste, thyme, and beef broth. Simmer for 8 minutes until the liquid reduces slightly.
Stir in the frozen peas and season with the remaining measured salt and black pepper.
Transfer the meat mixture to a 25cm baking dish.
Spread the mashed potatoes evenly over the meat, using a fork to create textured peaks.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling.
Divide into six portions. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; consume within 3-4 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C.
note: A warming European classic for cooling October evenings. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Cover tightly and refrigerate for up to 4 days. Can be frozen for up to 1 month; thaw in the refrigerator before reheating.

photo.author: Abhinaba Basu  from Redmond, United States
photo.alt: Rustic Root Vegetable Cottage Pie — illustrative photo

title: Herbed Goat Cheese Crostini
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C.
Brush baguette slices lightly with olive oil and place on a baking sheet.
Toast in the oven for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and crisp.
In a small bowl, whisk the goat cheese until creamy and fold in half the chives.
Spread approximately 10g of goat cheese onto each toasted baguette slice.
Top each slice with a small amount of crushed walnuts and a drizzle of honey.
Garnish each crostini with the remaining chopped chives, distributing them evenly among all eighteen pieces.
Serve three crostini per person. Refrigerate any leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days.
note: A sophisticated, simple snack using classic European ingredients. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Best served immediately. Keep toppings and bread separate if preparing ahead of time.

photo.author: Charles Haynes
photo.alt: Herbed Goat Cheese Crostini — illustrative photo

title: Miso Glazed Cod with Bok Choy
steps: Rinse rice and cook in a rice cooker or covered pot according to package instructions.
Whisk miso, glaze water, rice vinegar, and sugar in a bowl until smooth. Pat cod dry and coat with marinade; refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 400°F / 200°C. Line a large sheet pan with parchment paper.
Place cod on the pan and bake for 12-15 minutes until fish reaches 145°F / 63°C and flakes easily.
While fish bakes, trim bok choy, halve lengthwise, and wash thoroughly.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear bok choy cut-side down for 3 minutes until charred.
Add 30mL water to the skillet, cover, and steam for 2 minutes until tender.
Divide rice, bok choy, and cod among six bowls; serve immediately.
note: Ensure fish reaches internal temperature safely. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Store in airtight containers in refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C.

photo.author: Tiia Monto
photo.alt: Miso Glazed Cod with Bok Choy — illustrative photo

title: Sweet Potato Karinto
steps: Cut sweet potatoes into 1cm x 5cm sticks. Soak in cold water for 10 minutes to remove excess starch.
Pat sticks completely dry with a clean towel to prevent splattering.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 320°F / 160°C. Fry sticks in small batches for 6-8 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain fried potatoes on a wire rack or paper towels.
In a clean pan, combine sugar and water. Heat over medium until it bubbles and turns a light amber syrup.
Toss the fried potato sticks in the syrup until coated. Work quickly.
Spread on a parchment-lined tray and sprinkle immediately with sesame seeds.
Cool for 10 minutes until the sugar hardens. Serve in six small portions.
note: Ensure oil is handled safely during frying. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.

photo.author: Kurtkaiser
photo.alt: Sweet Potato Karinto — illustrative photo

title: Baked Mediterranean Sea Bass
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F / 200°C. Put couscous in a large heatproof bowl, add its measured boiling water, cover for 10 minutes and fluff with a fork; check the package liquid ratio and adjust if needed.
In a large bowl, toss tomatoes, olives, capers, onion, oil, and oregano.
Arrange the vegetable mixture on a large rimmed baking sheet.
Nestle the sea bass fillets among the vegetables. Top each fillet with a lemon slice.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until fish is opaque and reaches 145°F / 63°C.
Remove from oven and let rest for 3 minutes.
Divide into six portions, ensuring each serving gets a mix of vegetables and fish. Divide the couscous among all six plates and place the fish and cooked vegetables alongside.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
note: Check for stray olive pits. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 3 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C.

title: Spiced Roasted Broad Beans

ingredients.name: Canned cooked broad beans (fava), drained, skins removed

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F / 200°C.
Rinse the drained cooked beans, remove loose skins and pat them very dry; spread on a clean towel for 15 minutes to remove excess moisture.
In a bowl, toss the dry beans with olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, and salt.
Spread in a single layer on a large baking sheet. Use two trays if needed so that the beans do not crowd each other.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, shaking the pan every 10 minutes, until the outside is crisp. Larger beans may remain slightly tender inside; cool a sample before checking texture.
The beans should be crunchy but not burnt.
Cool completely on the pan, as they crisp up while cooling.
Divide into six small bowls for serving.
note: Ensure beans are thoroughly dried before oiling for maximum crunch. Use fully cooked beans, not raw or merely soaked dried beans. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Cool completely. Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 3 days; re-crisp in a 350°F / 175°C oven before serving.

photo.author: Alex Ex
photo.alt: Spiced Roasted Broad Beans — illustrative photo

title: Five-Spice Braised Pork Belly
steps: Cut pork belly into 4cm cubes. Blanch in boiling water for 3 minutes, drain, and pat dry.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add rock sugar and stir until melted and amber-colored.
Add pork to the pot, coating well with the sugar syrup. Add ginger, garlic, star anise, and cinnamon. Stir in the five-spice powder.
Stir in soy sauce and dark soy sauce. Pour in water until the meat is just covered.

Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce heat to low. Simmer for 75-80 minutes until the meat is fork-tender. Meanwhile, cook the rice with its measured water, following the package ratio; steam the washed bok choy for 5-7 minutes just before serving.
Remove the lid and increase heat to medium-high to reduce the sauce until thick and glossy, about 10 minutes.
Check internal temperature reaches 160°F/71°C. Remove spices.
Serve in six bowls garnished with scallions. Divide the rice and bok choy among the six bowls alongside the pork.
note: Best served with steamed bok choy to balance the richness. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container within 2 hours; consume within 3 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C.

photo.author: N509FZ
photo.alt: Five-Spice Braised Pork Belly — illustrative photo

title: Crispy Spiced Lotus Root Chips
steps: Slice peeled lotus root into very thin 2mm rounds. Soak in water for 10 minutes to remove excess starch.
Drain thoroughly and pat completely dry with paper towels.
Toss the slices in a bowl with cornstarch until lightly coated.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F/175°C. Fry slices in small batches for 3-5 minutes until golden and crisp.
Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on wire racks.
While still hot, sprinkle with the mixture of five-spice, salt, and white pepper.
Ensure all pieces are evenly seasoned.
Divide into six portions and serve immediately.
note: Lotus root is in peak season during autumn. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days; crisp in a 300°F/150°C oven if needed.

photo.author: Fumikas Sagisavas
photo.alt: Crispy Spiced Lotus Root Chips — illustrative photo

title: Taiwanese Oyster Omelet Style Egg Scramble
steps: Cook the rice with its measured water according to package directions. Gently rinse oysters in cold water and pat dry; keep chilled until each batch is cooked. Mix sweet potato starch with the measured slurry water.
Whisk eggs in a large bowl. Stir in the starch slurry and half the scallions.
Heat 10mL oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Sear a portion of oysters for 1 minute.
Pour one-sixth of the egg mixture over the oysters. Scatter a handful of bok choy on top.
Cook until the eggs are mostly set but still slightly soft in the center, about 3 minutes.
Flip carefully and continue cooking until the egg mixture reaches 160°F / 71°C throughout, with no runny egg remaining. Check the thickest part with a food thermometer.
Repeat for all six portions. Keep the remaining raw oyster mixture refrigerated between batches and use a clean spatula for finished portions.
Serve hot with a drizzle of sweet chili sauce. Divide the cooked rice among six plates alongside the scramble.
note: Sweet potato starch is essential for the authentic chewy texture. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container within 2 hours; consume within 2 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C.

photo.author: pelican  from Tokyo, Japan
photo.alt: Taiwanese Oyster Omelet Style Egg Scramble — illustrative photo

title: Brown Sugar Ginger Mochi Balls
steps: Combine glutinous rice flour and warm water in a bowl. Knead until a smooth, pliable dough forms.
Divide dough into 18 equal small balls (3 per person).
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Drop balls in and cook until they float, about 4-5 minutes.
In a separate small saucepan, simmer 200mL water, brown sugar, and ginger until reduced to a light syrup.
Drain the mochi balls and transfer them to a serving platter.
Pour the warm ginger syrup over the mochi balls.
Sprinkle with crushed peanuts.
Serve six portions immediately.
note: Serve warm as a traditional dessert snack. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Best eaten fresh. If stored, keep in syrup in the refrigerator for 1 day; warm gently in a microwave.

photo.author: cherrylet
photo.alt: Brown Sugar Ginger Mochi Balls — illustrative photo

title: Steamed Ginger Soy Cod
steps: Prepare a steamer setup by bringing a large pot of water to a boil. Cook the measured rice and rice water according to package instructions while preparing the fish.
Pat the cod fillets dry and place them on a heat-proof plate that fits inside your steamer.
Top the fish evenly with half of the ginger and half of the scallions.

Place the plate in the steamer, cover tightly, and steam for 8-10 minutes or until the fish reaches 145°F / 63°C. Avoid overlapping fillets; use two batches if the steamer is small. Steam broccoli on a separate rack or after the fish for 5-7 minutes until tender.
In a small saucepan, combine soy sauce, sugar, and water; simmer until sugar dissolves.
Remove fish from steamer, discard the excess liquid on the plate, and top with the remaining ginger and scallions.
Heat the neutral oil until shimmering, then remove it from the heat. Carefully spoon it over the ginger and scallions, keeping your hands away from any splashes.
Drizzle with the warm soy sauce mixture and garnish with cilantro before serving. Divide fish, rice and broccoli among six plates.
note: Use fresh, firm-fleshed white fish for the best texture. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container within 2 hours; consume within 2 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C.

title: Curry Fish Balls
steps: Heat oil in a wok or deep skillet over medium heat; add minced garlic and fry until fragrant.
Stir in curry powder and turmeric, cooking for 30 seconds to toast the spices.
Pour in coconut milk and water, stirring well to combine.
Add the frozen fish balls to the liquid and bring to a gentle simmer.

Cover and cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and coats the fish balls. Follow the fish-ball package cooking directions and verify the center reaches 165°F / 74°C, adding cooking time as needed.
Add the measured salt only after tasting the sauce, since packaged fish balls may already be salty.
Divide into six bowls and serve warm on skewers or with small forks.
allergens: Fish; commercial fish balls may also contain Wheat, Egg or Soy — check the label
note: Traditional Hong Kong street food style snack. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Store in refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat thoroughly to 165°F/74°C.

title: Spicy Braised Tofu and Pork
steps: Cook the measured rice and rice water according to package directions. In a large skillet, brown the ground pork over medium-high heat until it reaches 160°F / 71°C.
Add the onion and carrots and cook for 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the onion softens and carrots begin to become tender.
Whisk together gochujang, soy sauce, garlic, and sesame oil with the water.
Arrange the tofu slices on top of the cooked pork in the skillet.
Pour the sauce mixture over the tofu and pork.
Cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 12-15 minutes, allowing the tofu to absorb the sauce.
Remove the lid, sprinkle with scallions, and simmer for another 2 minutes to reduce the liquid slightly.
Divide the cooked rice among six bowls, then spoon the hot tofu, pork, carrots and sauce over each portion.
allergens: Soy, Sesame; gochujang and soy sauce may also contain Wheat — check labels
note: A hearty, comforting dish common in Korean home cooking. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C.

title: Sweet Potato Pancakes
steps: In a large bowl, combine the grated sweet potatoes, flour, sugar, and salt.
Gradually stir in the water until a thick, uniform batter forms.
Heat 20mL of oil in a large nonstick pan over medium heat.
Drop 1/4 cup portions of the batter into the pan, flattening them slightly with a spatula.
Cook for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden and crispy.
Remove and drain briefly on a paper towel.
Repeat with remaining batter, adding more oil as needed.
Serve warm drizzled with honey.
note: A popular sweet snack using seasonal autumn sweet potatoes. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 2 days; reheat in a pan or toaster oven to regain crispness.

title: Spiced Cauliflower and Potato Curry
steps: Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add onion and cook for 8 minutes until translucent. Stir in ginger and garlic, cooking for 1 minute.
Add turmeric, coriander, chili powder, and salt. Cook for 30 seconds, then add tomatoes.
Simmer tomatoes for 5 minutes until they break down into a thick paste.
Add cauliflower and potatoes to the pan, stirring to coat with the spice mixture.
Pour in water, cover tightly, and simmer over medium-low heat for 15-20 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Remove lid and cook for another 3-5 minutes to evaporate excess liquid if necessary.
Stir in fresh cilantro and divide into six bowls.
note: Serve with basmati rice or flatbread. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C.

title: Spiced Roasted Chickpeas

ingredients.name: Canned chickpeas, drained and patted dry

steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F / 200°C.
Ensure chickpeas are very dry by patting them with a paper towel; moisture prevents crispiness.
In a large bowl, toss the chickpeas with olive oil until evenly coated.
Spread chickpeas in a single layer on a large rimmed baking sheet.
Roast for 35-40 minutes, shaking the tray every 10 minutes, until chickpeas are golden and crunchy.
Remove from oven and immediately toss with garam masala, paprika, salt, and pepper while still hot.
Let cool for 10 minutes to finish crisping.
Divide into six small bowls.
note: Best eaten the same day for maximum crunch. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days.

title: Autumn Harvest Pumpkin Risotto

ingredients.name: Water, only if needed to loosen the risotto

steps: Heat vegetable broth in a pot and keep at a low simmer.
In a large wide pan, heat olive oil and 20g of butter over medium heat. Sauté onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and stir for 30 seconds without browning it.
Add rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly until edges are translucent.
Add 250mL of hot broth, stirring until absorbed. Continue adding broth in 250mL increments, stirring frequently, until rice is creamy but al dente (approx 20-25 minutes).
Fold in the pumpkin puree and cook for 3 minutes to heat through.
Remove from heat. Stir in the remaining butter, Parmesan, salt, and sage.
Check that the risotto is creamy; add a splash of water if needed.
Divide into six warm bowls.
note: Use fresh pumpkin if available, roasted and mashed. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C with a little water.

title: Roasted Apple and Walnut Medley
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C.
Toss the cubed apples with melted butter, maple syrup, and cinnamon in a large mixing bowl.
Spread apples in a single layer on a parchment-lined baking tray.
Roast for 20 minutes until apples are soft but not mushy.
Add walnuts to the tray and toss gently with the apples.
Roast for another 5 minutes until walnuts are toasted and fragrant.
Remove from oven and let cool slightly.
Divide into six small bowls and serve warm.
note: Suitable for a crisp autumn afternoon snack. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Store in the refrigerator for up to 2 days; reheat in a pan or microwave.

title: Smoky Black Bean and Corn Stuffed Peppers
steps: Cook brown rice with the measured water according to the package directions. Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C and halve peppers lengthwise, removing seeds.
Heat oil in a wide pan. Soften onion for 5 minutes, then stir in paprika, cumin, tomatoes and salt; simmer for 5 minutes.
Fold in the drained cooked beans, corn and cooked rice. Stir until the filling is hot throughout, adding no uncooked beans.
Arrange twelve pepper halves in two baking dishes. Divide filling evenly among them and cover the dishes loosely with foil.
Bake for 30 minutes. Remove foil, scatter cheese evenly and bake for another 10 minutes, until peppers are tender and filling reaches 165°F / 74°C.
Serve two pepper halves per person. Cool leftovers in shallow containers and refrigerate within 2 hours.
allergens: Milk; check canned products for additional allergens
note: Photo illustrates a similar dish; appearance and ingredients may differ. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate in shallow covered containers within 2 hours; use within 3 days. Reheat cooked leftovers to 165°F / 74°C.

title: Cinnamon Peanut Butter Oat Bites
steps: Check that the peanut butter contains no unexpected allergens. Combine oats, chopped raisins, chia seeds and cinnamon in a large bowl.
Stir peanut butter, honey and measured water together in a separate bowl until evenly blended; use room-temperature peanut butter to make mixing easier.
Add the wet mixture to the dry ingredients. Fold thoroughly until every patch of oats is moistened and the mixture holds together when squeezed.
Refrigerate the bowl for 20 minutes to let the oats and chia absorb moisture. Divide the mixture into eighteen equal portions.
Roll each portion into a compact ball with clean hands and arrange in a single layer in a covered container.
Serve three bites per person. Keep refrigerated and consume within 3 days; do not store these moist bites at room temperature.
allergens: Peanuts; oats may contain wheat unless certified gluten-free
note: Photo illustrates a similar dish; appearance and ingredients may differ. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish. Additional chilling time: 20 minutes.
storage: Keep covered and refrigerated; consume within 3 days. Serve cold. Allow 20 minutes of chilling.

title: Caramelized Onion and White Bean Skillet
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide heavy pan over medium-low heat. Add onions and cook for 20 minutes, stirring frequently, until soft and golden rather than scorched.
Add diced carrots and garlic. Cook for 5 minutes while stirring, then add thyme, stock and the drained, fully cooked beans.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered for 10 minutes until the carrots are tender and the sauce lightly thickens.
Fold in spinach in two batches, allowing it to wilt. Add lemon juice, salt and pepper; taste before adding any additional seasoning.
Toast the measured bread in a dry skillet or toaster. Divide the beans and vegetables among six shallow bowls and serve each with 60g bread.
Refrigerate the bean mixture within 2 hours; store bread separately so it keeps its texture.
allergens: Wheat in bread; stock may contain celery or other allergens
note: Photo illustrates a similar dish; appearance and ingredients may differ. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate in shallow covered containers within 2 hours; use within 3 days. Reheat cooked leftovers to 165°F / 74°C.

title: Apple and Raisin Hand Pies
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Put apples, raisins, sugar, lemon juice and cinnamon in a saucepan with 30mL water.
Simmer for 5 minutes. Mix cornstarch with the remaining water, stir into the fruit and cook for 1 minute until thickened. Spread filling on a plate and cool completely.
Keep pastry cold while cutting twelve equal rectangles. Spoon cooled filling onto six rectangles, leaving a clear 1cm border around the edges.
Cover each with another rectangle. Press edges firmly with a fork, cut two small steam vents in each top and transfer to a lined tray.
Brush with beaten egg. Bake for 20-25 minutes until deeply golden, with cooked pastry at the base and no wet egg glaze.
Cool for 10 minutes before serving one pie per person. Refrigerate any leftover pies within 2 hours.
allergens: Wheat, egg; pastry may contain milk or soy
note: Photo illustrates a similar dish; appearance and ingredients may differ. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.

title: Miso-Glazed Shiitake and Tofu Donburi

ingredients.name: Water mixed with rice vinegar (45mL water + 15mL rice vinegar)

steps: Rinse rice until water runs clear and cook in a rice cooker or covered pot using the 750mL water.
Whisk miso, the measured water-vinegar mixture, soy sauce, and sugar in a small bowl until smooth to create the glaze.
Heat 15mL oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the tofu cubes on all sides for about 6-8 minutes, then remove them from the pan.
Add the remaining 15mL oil to the same pan and sauté the shiitake mushrooms for 5 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Return the tofu to the pan with the mushrooms. Pour the miso glaze over the mixture and stir gently for 3-4 minutes until the sauce bubbles and coats the ingredients evenly.
Ensure the internal temperature of the tofu reaches 160°F / 71°C.
Divide the cooked rice into six deep bowls. Spoon the miso tofu and mushroom mixture generously over the rice.
Garnish with sliced scallions and serve immediately.
allergens: Soy, wheat in soy sauce; check miso label
note: Refrigerate any leftovers within 2 hours of cooking. Use within 3-4 days and reheat until steaming hot (165°F / 74°C). Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate rice and tofu in shallow covered containers within 2 hours; consume within 3 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C.

title: Nori-Crusted Crispy Rice Crackers
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F / 200°C and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a bowl, mix cold rice with shredded nori, soy sauce, sesame oil, and cornstarch until the rice is sticky and well-coated.
Spread the mixture onto the parchment paper in a very thin, even layer about 0.5cm thick.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, checking frequently, until the edges are golden brown and the center is completely crisp.
Remove from the oven and while still warm, sprinkle immediately with sesame seeds.
Let the sheet cool completely on the tray, as it will continue to harden and become crunchy.
Break the large sheet into smaller, irregular snack-sized shards.
Divide into six portions and serve.
allergens: Soy, sesame, wheat in soy sauce
note: Best enjoyed fresh for maximum crispness. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish. Use cold rice that was refrigerated within 2 hours after cooking; do not use rice left at room temperature overnight.
storage: Use promptly. Refrigerate within 2 hours, use within 3 days and reheat to 165°F / 74°C; rice snacks are not assumed shelf-stable.

title: Lemon-Garlic White Fish with Roasted Fennel
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Put couscous in a heatproof bowl, add the measured boiling water, cover for 5 minutes and fluff with a fork.
Place the fennel wedges and cherry tomatoes on a large rimmed baking sheet. Drizzle with 30mL of olive oil, sprinkle with half the salt and pepper, and toss to coat.
Roast the vegetables for 15 minutes until they begin to soften.
In a small bowl, whisk the remaining 30mL olive oil, garlic, lemon juice, and oregano.
Pat the fish dry and place the fillets on top of the vegetables. Brush the fish generously with the lemon-garlic mixture.
Return to the oven and roast for 10-12 minutes, or until the fish reaches an internal temperature of 145°F / 63°C and flakes easily with a fork.
Divide the couscous, roasted vegetables and fish among six plates.
Drizzle any remaining pan juices over the fish before serving.
note: Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours. Use within 3 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate fish and couscous within 2 hours; use within 3 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C.

title: Marinated Olive and Artichoke Medley

ingredients.name: Canned artichoke hearts, drained and halved

steps: Drain the artichoke hearts well and pat dry to ensure the marinade sticks.
In a medium bowl, combine the olives and artichoke hearts.
Add the olive oil, lemon zest, fresh rosemary, sliced garlic, and red pepper flakes.
Toss everything together until the ingredients are thoroughly coated in the oil and herbs.
Cover the bowl and let the mixture sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
If preparing ahead, refrigerate for up to 24 hours and bring to room temperature before serving.
Divide into six small bowls for serving.
Serve with toothpicks for easy snacking.
note: This snack is best when allowed to marinate for at least 30 minutes. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Store in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.

title: Autumn Mushroom and Ginger Braised Chicken
steps: Rinse the measured rice and cook with 600mL rice water according to package instructions.
Heat oil in a large wok or heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add ginger and garlic, stir-frying for 1 minute until highly aromatic.
Add chicken pieces to the pan. Sear for 5-6 minutes until lightly browned on all sides.
Add sliced mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes until softened. Stir in the sugar, soy sauce, and dark soy sauce, coating the chicken evenly.
Pour in the water and bring to a gentle boil. Reduce heat to low, cover with a lid, and simmer for 20-25 minutes.
Remove the lid and increase the heat to medium-high for 5 minutes, stirring frequently to reduce the sauce until it becomes thick and glossy.
Check that chicken reaches 165°F / 74°C. Remove from heat and stir in half the scallions.
Divide rice into six bowls, top with the chicken and mushroom mixture, and garnish with remaining scallions.
note: Use fresh shiitake if available for a deeper autumn flavor profile. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container within 2 hours. Consume within 3-4 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C.

title: Crispy Five-Spice Tofu Bites

ingredients.name: Extra firm tofu, pressed and 2cm cubes

steps: Pat pressed tofu cubes extremely dry with a clean kitchen towel to ensure crispiness.
In a shallow bowl, toss tofu cubes with cornstarch until every side is evenly coated; shake off excess.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 350°F / 175°C. Test temperature with a small piece of tofu; it should sizzle immediately.
Fry the tofu in three batches to avoid overcrowding the pan, cooking for 5-6 minutes per batch until golden and crispy.
Remove tofu using a slotted spoon and drain on a wire rack for 2 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together the five-spice powder, salt, and white pepper.
While the tofu is still hot, sprinkle the seasoning mixture over the bites and toss gently.
Divide into six small bowls and serve immediately while hot and crunchy.
note: Pressing the tofu for at least 30 minutes before cutting is essential for texture. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours; use within 3 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C before serving.

title: Taiwanese Braised Pork Rice Bowls
steps: Cook the 450g rice with 600mL rice water according to package instructions.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, brown the ground pork over medium heat until it reaches 160°F / 71°C. Remove pork and set aside.
In the same pot, fry shallots and garlic in the rendered pork fat until golden brown.
Return pork to the pot. Stir in the rock sugar, soy sauce, deglazing water, and five-spice powder.
Pour in water, bring to a simmer, and cook covered on low heat for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove the lid and simmer for another 10-15 minutes until the sauce is thick and flavorful.
While the meat finishes, steam the bok choy until tender.
Divide rice into six bowls, top with the braised pork mixture, and serve with a side of steamed bok choy.
note: The key to this dish is the slow reduction of the sauce to develop a deep, savory flavor. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container within 2 hours. Consume within 3-4 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C.

title: Sweet Potato and Scallion Fritters
steps: In a large bowl, combine the shredded sweet potato, scallions, flour, cornstarch, and salt.
Gradually stir in the water until a thick, cohesive batter forms; the mixture should bind the potatoes together.
Heat 20mL of oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Scoop 1/6 of the batter into the pan for each fritter, flattening with a spatula to about 10cm diameter.
Cook for 5-6 minutes per side until the sweet potato is tender and the edges are deeply golden and crispy.
Remove from the pan and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil.
Repeat for all six fritters, adding remaining oil as necessary.
Serve warm, cut into wedges if desired.
note: Ensure the sweet potato is shredded finely so it cooks through quickly. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours; consume within 3 days. Reheat in a 350°F / 175°C oven for 8-10 minutes to restore crispness.

title: Tomato and Egg Noodle Bowls
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook noodles according to package directions, adding bok choy for the last 2 minutes, then drain well.
Beat eggs with salt. Heat 30mL oil in a wide nonstick pan and scramble the eggs gently until fully set; transfer to a clean bowl.
Add remaining oil and tomato wedges to the pan. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until tomatoes begin releasing juice.
Stir in soy sauce, sugar and the measured sauce water. Simmer for 3 minutes, then return cooked eggs and fold gently into the tomatoes.
Heat the combined egg mixture to 160°F / 71°C. Divide noodles and bok choy among six bowls and spoon the tomato-egg sauce over them.
Scatter scallions across the bowls. Serve immediately and refrigerate leftovers in shallow containers within 2 hours.
note: Photo illustrates a similar dish; appearance and ingredients may differ. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.

title: Sesame Coconut Pudding Squares
steps: Line a 20cm square shallow container with parchment paper, leaving edges overhanging so the set pudding can be lifted out safely.
Whisk cornstarch with 150mL of the cold milk in a small bowl until no lumps remain. Combine remaining milk, coconut milk and sugar in a saucepan.
Warm the saucepan over medium-low heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. Pour in the cornstarch mixture slowly while whisking continuously.
Cook gently for 3-5 minutes until the pudding thickens and bubbles. Keep stirring to prevent sticking, then fold in the toasted sesame seeds.
Pour into the lined container and smooth the top. Cool briefly, refrigerate within 2 hours and chill for at least 4 hours until firm.
Lift out, cut eighteen squares and coat lightly with shredded coconut. Serve three squares per person and keep all remaining pudding refrigerated.
note: Photo illustrates a similar dish; appearance and ingredients may differ. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish. Allow at least 4 hours of chilling beyond preparation and cooking.

title: Soy Garlic Chicken and Cabbage Rice Bowls

ingredients.name: Boneless chicken thighs, cut into 3cm pieces

steps: Cook rice with the measured rice water according to the package instructions. Mix soy sauce, garlic, ginger, sugar and sauce water in a bowl.
Heat oil in a wide deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken in two batches and brown for 4 minutes per batch, then return all chicken to the pan.
Add cabbage and carrots. Stir for 3 minutes to begin softening the vegetables, then pour the soy-garlic mixture over everything.
Reduce heat, cover and simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Check several chicken pieces with a food thermometer; each must reach 165°F / 74°C.
Remove the lid and simmer briefly if the sauce is too thin. Divide rice among six bowls and add equal portions of chicken and vegetables.
Garnish with scallions and sesame seeds. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat to 165°F / 74°C.

note: Photo illustrates a similar dish; appearance and ingredients may differ. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.

title: Crunchy Seaweed and Rice Puff Clusters
steps: Preheat the oven to 300°F / 150°C. Line a large shallow tray with baking parchment and measure the cereal into a heatproof mixing bowl.
Cut toasted nori into very small pieces using clean kitchen scissors. Toss through the cereal with the toasted sesame seeds so the dry mixture is evenly distributed.
Warm brown rice syrup, soy sauce and oil in a small saucepan over low heat for 1 minute, just until easy to stir; do not boil vigorously.
Pour the warm syrup over the cereal and immediately fold with a spatula until coated. Spread thinly on the lined tray without packing it into a thick slab.
Bake for 15 minutes, stirring once halfway through. Let cool completely on the tray so the mixture firms into crisp clusters.
Break into eighteen small clusters and divide three per person. Store only fully dry, crisp clusters in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.
allergens: Sesame, soy, wheat in soy sauce; check cereal label
note: Photo illustrates a similar dish; appearance and ingredients may differ. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Only fully dry, crisp clusters may be stored in an airtight container at room temperature, for up to 3 days. Refrigerate any softened or damp batch.

title: Coconut Tamarind Fish Curry

ingredients.name: Firm white fish fillets (e.g., cod or snapper), 3cm cubes

steps: Cook the rice and measured rice water according to package directions. Heat oil in a large deep pan over medium-high heat. Add mustard seeds and wait for them to pop, then add curry leaves and onions.
Sauté onions for 7 minutes until golden, then stir in ginger, garlic, turmeric, and chili powder; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Whisk tamarind paste with water and add to the pan along with the coconut milk and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add fish pieces carefully into the sauce. Do not stir vigorously as this will break the fish.
Simmer covered for 8-10 minutes. Check that the fish reaches 145°F / 63°C and flakes easily with a fork.
Fold spinach into the curry for 2 minutes to wilt it, then remove from heat once fish reaches 145°F / 63°C.
Divide cooked rice into six bowls and spoon equal portions of fish, spinach and curry sauce over each.
Serve hot immediately. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours, use within 3 days, and reheat to 165°F / 74°C.
note: Serve with steamed basmati rice. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

title: Spiced Peanut Sundal
steps: Heat oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add mustard seeds and wait until they pop.
Add urad dal and fry for 1 minute until golden brown, then add curry leaves, green chili, and asafoetida.
Add the roasted peanuts to the skillet and toss well to coat them in the tempered spices.
Cook for 3-4 minutes on low heat to ensure the peanuts are warm and aromatic.
Stir in the grated coconut and salt, tossing for another 1 minute.
Remove from heat and let sit for 2 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Divide into six small bowls for serving.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours, use within 2 days, and reheat cooked leftovers to 165°F / 74°C.
allergens: Peanuts, mustard; asafoetida blends may contain wheat
note: A traditional South Indian protein-rich snack. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours because this snack contains fresh coconut; use within 2 days.

title: Roasted Root Vegetable and Lentil Medley
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Toss parsnips, carrots, and beets with 30mL oil, salt, and pepper on two large baking sheets.
Roast for 35-40 minutes, turning halfway through, until the vegetables are tender and caramelized at the edges.
While vegetables roast, place lentils and broth in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 25-30 minutes until tender but not mushy.
Drain any excess broth from the lentils and transfer them to a large mixing bowl.
Whisk the remaining 15mL oil with balsamic vinegar and thyme; pour over the warm lentils.
Fold the roasted vegetables into the lentils gently.
Divide into six plates and top with chopped walnuts.
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours, use within 4 days, and reheat to 165°F / 74°C.
note: A hearty autumn dish focusing on root vegetables. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

title: Spiced Pear and Oat Crumble Pots
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Toss diced pears with lemon juice, vanilla, and 15mL maple syrup in a bowl.
Divide the pear mixture among six small oven-safe ramekins.
In a separate bowl, combine oats, almond flour, and cinnamon. Rub in the chilled butter with your fingers until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs.
Stir in the remaining maple syrup into the crumble topping.
Sprinkle the topping evenly over the pears in each ramekin.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until the fruit is bubbling and the topping is golden brown.
Remove from the oven and let cool for 5 minutes before serving.
Store leftovers in the refrigerator for up to 3 days; reheat in the oven or microwave.
note: Perfect for a crisp October evening. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested. Photo illustrates a similar dish.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

title: Harvest Turkey and Apple Skillet
steps: Cook the measured rice with its separate 600mL water according to package directions. Heat oil in a large 30cm skillet over medium-high heat. Add turkey and cook until browned, reaching 165°F/74°C; break into pieces as you cook.
Add onion and celery to the skillet. Sauté for 6-8 minutes until the vegetables soften and become fragrant.
Stir in the diced apples, dried cranberries, sage, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 3-4 minutes until apples begin to soften slightly.
Pour in the chicken broth, scraping the bottom of the pan to release any browned bits. Reduce heat to medium.
Simmer for 10-12 minutes, uncovered, allowing the liquid to reduce by half and flavors to meld.
Verify the internal temperature of the turkey again to ensure it remains at or above 165°F/74°C.
Remove from heat and let sit for 3 minutes before serving.
Divide into six bowls. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; consume within 3-4 days, reheating to 165°F/74°C.
note: Serve alongside warm crusty bread or over quinoa. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate turkey and rice in shallow covered containers within 2 hours; use within 3-4 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C. Freeze cooled portions for up to 1 month.

title: Maple Pecan Popcorn Clusters
steps: Preheat the oven to 325°F / 163°C and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Place the popped popcorn and chopped pecans in a large mixing bowl.
In a small saucepan, combine maple syrup and butter over medium heat. Bring to a gentle simmer for 2 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir the cinnamon and salt into the syrup mixture.
Pour the hot syrup over the popcorn and pecans. Toss quickly and thoroughly with a silicone spatula until every piece is coated.
Spread the mixture evenly in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the coating is golden and tacky.
Remove from oven and let cool completely on the tray, as the clusters will harden while cooling. Divide into six portions.
note: Ensure popcorn is fully cooled before storing to maintain crispness. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.

title: Braised Leek and White Bean Stew
steps: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the sliced leeks and cook for 10-12 minutes until very soft, stirring occasionally to prevent browning.
Stir in the garlic and fresh thyme; cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the drained cannellini beans and stir to coat them with the leeks.
Pour in the vegetable stock. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, uncovered, for 20 minutes.
Stir in the heavy cream and cook for another 5 minutes until the stew thickens slightly.
Remove from heat and stir in the lemon juice, salt, and black pepper.
Ensure the stew is heated through to at least 165°F/74°C.
Divide into six bowls. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; consume within 3-4 days, reheating to 165°F/74°C. Serve each bowl with 60g of the measured bread.
allergens: Milk, wheat; check stock and bread labels
note: Serve with crusty baguette. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate stew in shallow covered containers within 2 hours; use within 3-4 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C. Freeze stew without bread for up to 1 month.

title: Crispy Polenta Sticks with Tomato Dip
steps: Bring the measured 800mL water to a boil in a 3L saucepan. Slowly whisk in the cornmeal and salt to prevent lumps.
Reduce to low heat and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring continuously with a long-handled spoon until thick and pulling away from the sides.
Spread into a parchment-lined 20cm square tray about 2cm deep. Cool, then refrigerate for 45 minutes until firm enough to slice cleanly.
Preheat the oven to 400°F/200°C. Cut the slab into eighteen sticks and arrange on a lined baking sheet with space between them.
Brush every side with the measured olive oil. Bake for 20-25 minutes, turning halfway, until the edges are crisp and golden.
Meanwhile simmer crushed tomatoes and oregano in a small saucepan for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Divide three sticks and one-sixth of the dip among each of six plates.
note: Polenta must be fully cooled before slicing. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate cooked leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours; use within 2 days. Reheat until the center reaches 165°F/74°C. Freeze cooled portions for up to 1 month, thaw in the refrigerator and reheat thoroughly.

title: Simmered Ginger Pork and Daikon
steps: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Brown the pork cubes in two batches until seared, about 5 minutes per batch; remove to a plate.
In the same pot, add daikon and ginger, sautéing for 3 minutes until the daikon edges become slightly translucent.
Return pork to the pot. Add the measured 560mL braising water, soy sauce, sugar and rice vinegar; stir once to combine.

Cover and simmer gently for 60-75 minutes until pork and daikon are fork-tender. Meanwhile cook the measured rice with its separate 600mL water according to package directions and steam bok choy until tender.
Remove the lid and simmer for another 5-7 minutes to reduce the sauce until it becomes glossy and coats the pork.
Verify that the pork reaches an internal temperature of 160°F/71°C.
Divide the cooked rice and bok choy among six bowls, then add equal portions of pork and daikon.
Garnish with sliced scallions before serving.
allergens: Soy, wheat (unless gluten-free soy sauce is used)
note: The daikon absorbs the savory-sweet braising liquid, making it very tender. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container within 2 hours; consume within 3-4 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C.

title: Savory Steamed Egg Cups with Mushrooms
steps: Bring 1L water to a simmer in a covered steamer. Choose six 150mL heatproof ramekins and arrange them so steam can circulate around each cup.
Trim the mushrooms and slice them thinly. Divide the measured mushrooms evenly among the six ramekins, leaving ample room for the egg mixture.
Whisk all six eggs with the measured 300mL water, soy sauce and salt until combined, avoiding vigorous beating that creates excessive bubbles.
Strain through a fine sieve into a pitcher. Pour evenly into the ramekins, filling no more than two-thirds full; loosely cover each cup with foil.
Place cups above the simmering water, cover the steamer and cook gently for 15-20 minutes. Check the center of each custard reaches 160°F/71°C.
Turn off the heat and carefully lift out the cups with oven mitts. Rest for 3 minutes, then serve one custard per person while warm.
allergens: Eggs, soy, wheat unless gluten-free soy sauce is used
note: Straining the eggs is crucial for a silken texture. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours; consume within 2 days. Reheat to 165°F / 74°C.

title: Lemon-Herb Roasted Orzo and Chicken
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F/200°C. In a large oven-safe baking dish, combine dry orzo, cherry tomatoes, zucchini, garlic, half the oil, and half the oregano.
Pour the chicken broth over the orzo mixture, stirring to combine.
Toss chicken cubes with the remaining oil, remaining oregano, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Nestle the seasoned chicken cubes evenly on top of the orzo and vegetable mixture.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for another 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed by the orzo and the chicken reaches 165°F/74°C.
Remove from the oven, let rest for 5 minutes, and fluff the orzo with a fork.
Divide into six bowls, ensuring each serving has a portion of chicken and vegetables.
note: This one-dish meal allows the orzo to cook in the flavorful chicken juices. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers in shallow covered containers within 2 hours; use within 3 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C. Freeze cooled portions for up to 1 month; thaw in the refrigerator.

title: Roasted Pepper and Feta Pastry Pinwheels
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F/200°C and line two large baking sheets. Keep the puff pastry chilled until you are ready to roll it out.
Drain the roasted peppers thoroughly and pat dry; excess liquid makes the pastry soggy. Crumble the measured feta into small pieces.
Roll pastry into a 30cm by 40cm rectangle on its own parchment. Distribute peppers, feta and oregano evenly, leaving a 2cm border on one long edge.
Roll tightly toward that edge, pressing the seam closed. Refrigerate the log for 15 minutes, then use a sharp knife to cut eighteen equal slices.
Arrange slices cut-side up with 4cm space between them. Beat the measured egg and brush lightly over the exposed pastry edges.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, rotating trays halfway, until pastry is puffed, golden and cooked through in the center. Cool for 5 minutes and serve three pinwheels per person.
note: Keep pastry cold to ensure proper puffing. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate cooked leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours; use within 2 days. Reheat until the center reaches 165°F/74°C. Freeze cooled portions for up to 1 month, thaw in the refrigerator and reheat thoroughly.

title: Sesame Steamed Chicken with Napa Cabbage and Rice
steps: Rinse the measured rice and cook with its separate rice water in a covered pot or rice cooker following the package timing. Keep covered until serving.
Slice boneless chicken thighs into strips about 1cm thick. In a bowl toss evenly with the measured soy sauce, sesame oil and minced ginger.
Wash napa cabbage carefully and cut into 3cm pieces. Arrange in a wide heatproof dish that fits inside your steamer, allowing room around the dish.
Spread chicken strips over the cabbage in a shallow even layer. Do not mound the meat; use two dishes if necessary to ensure even cooking.
Bring the steamer water to a steady simmer. Cover and steam for 20-25 minutes, checking several thick chicken pieces reach 165°F/74°C; extend cooking if required.
Lift the dish out with oven mitts, avoiding hot steam. Fluff the rice and divide rice, cabbage and chicken equally among six bowls, spooning over the cooked juices.
allergens: Soy, sesame, wheat unless gluten-free soy sauce is used
note: Steam in batches if the dish does not fit in the steamer. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers in shallow covered containers within 2 hours; use within 3 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C. Freeze cooled portions for up to 1 month; thaw in the refrigerator.

title: Five-Spice Baked Chestnuts
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F/200°C. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment and separate the cooked peeled chestnuts, discarding any moldy or sour-smelling pieces.
Place the measured water and sugar in a small saucepan. Warm over low heat for 2 minutes, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in five-spice powder, neutral oil and salt to make a thin aromatic coating.
Put chestnuts into a mixing bowl. Pour over the coating and fold gently with a spatula so the soft nuts remain mostly whole.
Spread in one layer on the baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, turning gently halfway, until hot throughout and slightly browned at the edges.
Let stand for 5 minutes, then divide into six equal snack portions. Serve warm; refrigerate remaining cooked chestnuts within 2 hours rather than storing at room temperature.
note: Scoring is essential for safety and ease of peeling. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate cooked leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours; use within 2 days. Reheat until the center reaches 165°F/74°C. Freeze cooled portions for up to 1 month, thaw in the refrigerator and reheat thoroughly.

title: Taiwanese Pumpkin Rice Noodles with Shrimp
steps: Soak the measured rice noodles in warm water for the package recommended time, usually 5-10 minutes, until pliable. Drain well and cut into manageable lengths.
Heat the measured neutral oil in a large 30cm wok over medium-high heat. Add shredded pumpkin and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until beginning to soften.
Add peeled shrimp in an even layer. Turn and cook for 2-3 minutes until opaque, checking the thickest shrimp reaches 145°F/63°C.
Add drained noodles, soy sauce and the measured 300mL water. Use tongs to gently lift and turn the noodles without crushing the pumpkin.
Cook for another 4-5 minutes until noodles are tender and the measured liquid is absorbed. Lower the heat if noodles begin sticking to the wok.
Thinly slice the scallions and fold them through the hot noodles. Divide noodles, pumpkin and shrimp evenly among six bowls and serve immediately.
allergens: Shellfish, soy, wheat unless gluten-free soy sauce is used
note: Do not overcook the noodles to maintain texture. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers in shallow covered containers within 2 hours; use within 3 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C. Freeze cooled portions for up to 1 month; thaw in the refrigerator.

title: Taiwanese Taro and Peanut Sweet Soup
steps: Place the raw peanuts in a bowl, cover with ample cool water and refrigerate for 8 hours. Drain and rinse before cooking; discard the soaking water.
Put peanuts and the measured 1200mL fresh water into a 3L saucepan. Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 75-90 minutes until a peanut is tender when pressed with a fork. Check the pot periodically to prevent scorching or excessive evaporation.
Peel taro carefully and cut into 2cm cubes. Add to the tender peanuts and simmer for 20-25 minutes until completely cooked and easily pierced with a fork.
Stir in the measured sugar and coconut milk. Simmer gently for another 3 minutes, stirring to dissolve sugar without breaking up all the taro.
Divide taro, peanuts and broth equally among six bowls. Serve warm and refrigerate remaining soup within 2 hours; reheat thoroughly before serving again.
note: Soak peanuts for 8 hours in the refrigerator before cooking; soaking time is additional to active preparation. Taro must be fully cooked and never eaten raw. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate cooked leftovers in a covered container within 2 hours; use within 2 days. Reheat until the center reaches 165°F/74°C. Freeze cooled portions for up to 1 month, thaw in the refrigerator and reheat thoroughly.

title: Hong Kong Beef and Tomato Macaroni Soup
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the measured macaroni and cook for the package timing until just tender, then drain well.
Meanwhile heat the measured oil in a 4L saucepan over medium-high heat. Add ground beef and break it into small pieces with a spoon.
Cook for 6-8 minutes, stirring frequently, until beef is browned and reaches 160°F/71°C. Wash utensils that touched raw meat before using them for serving.
Add the chopped tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until softened, scraping the bottom to release browned pieces without burning them.
Pour in beef broth and soy sauce. Bring to a boil, lower to a steady simmer and cook for 5 minutes so the tomato flavor develops.
Add drained macaroni and heat for 2 minutes. Divide pasta, beef, tomatoes and broth evenly among six bowls; keep leftovers chilled and reheat to 165°F/74°C.
note: This is a classic Hong Kong breakfast style dish. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers in shallow covered containers within 2 hours; use within 3 days. Reheat to 165°F/74°C. Freeze cooled portions for up to 1 month; thaw in the refrigerator.

title: Hong Kong Baked Coconut Custard Tarts

ingredients.name: Unbaked mini tart shells, about 4cm diameter

steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F/190°C. Arrange eighteen unbaked mini tart shells, each about 4cm across, on a rimmed baking sheet or in a mini tart pan.
Whisk the measured coconut milk, sugar, eggs and cornstarch in a pitcher until smooth, making sure no dry cornstarch lumps remain.
Pour the custard evenly into the shells, stopping just below each pastry rim so the filling can expand without spilling onto the tray.
Place the tray on the middle oven rack. Bake for 20-25 minutes until the pastry is golden and custard has set with a slight center wobble.
Check the center of the custard reaches 160°F/71°C using a food thermometer. Extend baking briefly if needed, watching the pastry edges carefully.
Cool on the tray for 10 minutes, then move to a rack. Serve three tarts per person and refrigerate remaining tarts within 2 hours.
allergens: Eggs, wheat; tart shells may contain milk or soy, check label
note: Do not overfill the tart shells. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours; consume within 2 days.

title: Korean Soybean Paste Mushroom and Zucchini Stew with Barley
steps: Rinse the measured pearled barley in a sieve. Place in a 3L saucepan with its separate 2L water and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a gentle simmer and cook for 35-45 minutes or the package timing until tender but slightly chewy. Drain any excess cooking water.
Meanwhile bring the measured 800mL stew water to a boil in another 3L pot. Whisk in the doenjang until evenly dissolved without large lumps.
Add sliced mushrooms and diced zucchini. Lower the heat and simmer for 10-12 minutes until the vegetables are tender but still hold their shape.
Add the measured tofu and simmer for another 5 minutes until hot throughout. Stir gently to avoid breaking the tofu and scatter over scallions.
Divide cooked barley among six bowls and ladle equal portions of tofu, vegetables and broth alongside it. Serve hot and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
allergens: Soy, gluten (barley); check doenjang for wheat
note: Doenjang varies in saltiness; taste before adding extra salt. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.

title: Korean Steamed Apple and Cinnamon Rice Cakes
steps: Bring water to a simmer in a steamer. Line a 20cm heatproof cake pan with perforated parchment so steam can reach the rice mixture.
Peel and core the measured apples, then dice into 5mm pieces. Keep the pieces small so they become tender during the short steaming time.
In a mixing bowl combine rice flour, sugar and cinnamon. Sprinkle over the measured 180mL water gradually, rubbing the mixture between your fingers.
The mixture should form moist crumbs that hold together when squeezed, rather than a liquid batter. Fold through the diced apples until evenly distributed.
Spoon loosely into the lined pan in a layer no deeper than 2cm. Cover the steamer and cook for 25-30 minutes until no chalky raw flour remains.
Carefully remove the pan and rest for 10 minutes. Cut into six portions and serve warm; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and steam thoroughly when reheating.
note: Use regular non-glutinous rice flour, not sweet rice flour; the texture is a tender steamed cake rather than stretchy mochi. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.

title: Indian Spinach and Paneer with Cumin Rice
steps: Rinse the measured basmati rice. Put into a covered saucepan with its separate rice water and half the cumin seeds; cook according to package timing.
Heat the measured oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat. Add the remaining cumin seeds and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant without scorching.
Add diced onion and cook for 5-6 minutes until softened. Stir in garlic and ginger and cook for another minute, scraping the pan gently.
Add diced tomatoes, salt and the measured 100mL spinach water. Simmer for 5 minutes until tomatoes break down into a loose sauce.
Add washed spinach in batches, turning each batch until wilted. Stir in paneer cubes and simmer gently for 5-7 minutes until cheese is hot throughout.
Fluff the cumin rice and divide among six plates. Spoon equal amounts of spinach, paneer and sauce over each serving and serve hot.
note: Paneer does not melt; it holds its shape. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.

title: Crispy Spiced Lentil Crisps
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F / 200°C. Line two large baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a food processor, pulse lentils until coarsely mashed.
Transfer to a bowl and add chickpea flour, oil, cumin, chili powder, and salt. Mix well.
Gradually add water until a thick, spreadable dough forms.
Spread the dough very thinly across the parchment paper using a spatula to ensure even crisping.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, rotating trays halfway, until the edges are deep golden and the center is completely crisp.
Let cool completely on the trays; the crisps will firm up as they lose heat.
Break into irregular shards and divide into six portions.
note: A protein-rich, crunchy snack that pairs well with cooling yogurt dips. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered container within 2 hours; use within 3 days. Reheat at 350°F/175°C until the center reaches 165°F/74°C. Do not assume these homemade crisps are shelf-stable.

title: Autumn Harvest Roast Chicken with Root Vegetables
steps: Preheat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Prepare two large rimmed baking sheets.
Toss sweet potatoes, parsnips, and onions with 30mL oil, half the rosemary, and half the salt/pepper.
Spread vegetables on the trays and roast for 15 minutes.
While vegetables roast, pat chicken dry. Rub with remaining oil, rosemary, salt, pepper, and apple cider vinegar.
Remove trays from oven, nestle chicken and garlic cloves among the vegetables, ensuring everything is in a single layer.
Roast for 30–35 minutes, turning vegetables once, until chicken reaches 165°F/74°C and skin is golden.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Divide chicken and roasted vegetables among six plates.
note: A hearty, rustic meal celebrating peak autumn root produce. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.

title: Pumpkin and Sunflower Seed Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F/190°C and line a standard twelve-cup muffin tin with paper liners. This recipe makes twelve muffins, two per person.
Whisk the eggs, pumpkin puree, measured oil and milk in a large mixing bowl until smooth, making sure no streaks of egg remain.
In another bowl combine flour, baking powder, sugar, cinnamon and salt. Stir thoroughly so the baking powder is distributed evenly throughout the flour.
Fold the dry mixture gently into the wet ingredients until just combined. Stir in sunflower seeds, avoiding overmixing which makes muffins tough.
Divide batter evenly among twelve cups, filling each about three-quarters full. Bake for 22-25 minutes until tops spring back and a toothpick emerges clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack. Serve two muffins per person; refrigerate cooled leftovers within 2 hours.
note: Ensure baking powder is fresh to guarantee proper rise. Developed for James Real. Not kitchen-tested.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container within 2 hours; use within 3 days. Freeze cooled muffins for up to 1 month.
